newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO STOCKS EXTEND SLIDE ON U.S. LONG BOND, DOW.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO STOCKS EXTEND SLIDE ON U.S. LONG BOND, DOW.

text.p: Profit-taking in the wake of tumbling U.S. share and bond prices sharply extended losses on the Mexican bourse in late morning trade, dealers said.
"The U.S. long bond has triggered profit-taking, and the Dow has, too, but we're not seeing a sell-off. Dealing is really quite slow," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was down 77.98 points, or 1.50 percent, at 5,117.31. Trading volume was much slower than for many recent sessions at 30.3 million shares traded.
Dealers said profit-taking was most notable on market heavyweights Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) and Bancomer.
Telecomms firm Telmex shares had slid 40 centavos to 21.10 pesos, in tandem with its ADRs, off 1-3/8 to 53-13/16, themselves hauled down by the Dow Jones, which had dropped 157.48 points to 8,030.52.

Financial firm Bancomer had shed 16 centavos to 5.10 pesos. Dealers said the stock had fallen on profit-taking after recent sharp gains combined with fears higher interest rates would lead to a decline in loan quality at the firm's banking division.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were down 41/32 to yield 6.62 percent.
On the broad market scoreboard, sliders far outpaced gainers, by 72 to six, out of a total of 97 stocks that had changed hands.
